title: Request context propagation and weighted burn-rate for multi-tenant SLOs
creator: Amina Chowdhury
description: Implement request-level context propagation (hashed tenant id, route, and request-weight metadata) through tracing hooks and the metrics pipeline so burn-rate alerts compute weighted error/latency budgets per-tenant and per-route. Replace current coarse tenant-agnostic burn-rate with a two-layer approach: lightweight tenant-aware burn-rate for immediate paging decisions and a downstream aggregated burn-rate used by anomaly detector models for systemic incidents. Ensure tracing overhead stays within budget via adaptive sampling and header compression.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks propagate hashed tenant_id, route, and weight header for >=90% of incoming requests after rollout
Weighted burn-rate metric (burn_rate.weighted) is emitted for each tenant-route pair and accepted by alerting engine
Dashboard shows latency and error burn-rate heatmap by tenant and route and supports zooming to a single tenant
Alerting rules use weighted burn-rate to reduce noisy paging for low-weight tenants and trigger escalation only for aggregate/systemic anomalies
Automated integration tests validate propagation and correct weighted math (unit tests + e2e against staging pipeline)
Runbook updated with new playbook describing tenant-level vs systemic paging flows and mitigation steps
tasks: Add tracing hook in edge-proxy to attach x-rw-hash-tenant and x-rw-req-weight headers (PR #14523)
Extend trace-enricher service to read and persist tenant context to span tags and metrics (PR #14589)
Modify metrics-ingestor to compute burn_rate.weighted = sum(weighted_errors)/budget for tenant-route windows
Add adaptive sampling logic to avoid high-cardinality explosion in traces (config flag runtime.adaptive_trace_sampling)
Create SLO dashboard panels: tenant heatmap, p50/p95 by model+route, burn-rate trend and anomaly overlays
Author integration tests and load test scenario to validate no >5% throughput regression
comments: 2026-02-16 - Amina: Kickoff meeting notes posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Context+Propagation+and+Weighted+Burn+Rate
2026-02-22 - Jordan: Prototype implemented in edge-proxy; initial headers are x-rw-hash-tenant and x-rw-req-weight. Using SipHash for tenant hashing to avoid PII leakage.
2026-02-27 - Engineering review: Concern about cardinality when combining tenant+route+model. Decision: emit weighted metric only for route-level aggregation and sample traces on detailed spans.
2026-03-02 - QA: Integration test scaffold added. Found bug where 0 weight requests were being ignored instead of counted; fixed edge-proxy normalization code (PR #14610)
2026-03-10 - Jordan: Canaries show 92% coverage for header propagation and no measurable latency increase (+0.8ms median). Preparing alerting rules for canary alert window.
runbook_updates: New section: tenant-vs-systemic-paging - explains when to page on tenant-level weighted burn-rate vs when to wait for aggregate anomalies
Playbook step: if burn_rate.weighted fires for a single tenant with weight<0.05, mute paging and file follow-up ticket
Escalation matrix: tenant-impacted -> SE on-call -> Observability owner -> Platform PM
notes: Trade-offs: Per-tenant metrics improve signal fidelity but increase cardinality on metrics backend. Mitigation: only emit weighted burn-rate at the route aggregation level and use sampling for span-level details.
Privacy: Tenant ids are hashed with SipHash and truncated to 64-bit to avoid PII in telemetry. Legal reviewed approach on 2026-02-24.
Anomaly detection integration: downstream detector will consume aggregated weighted-burn metrics; detector model retraining scheduled in Cycle 12 to incorporate new features.
Future work: expose tenant-weighted SLOs in Console for customers to opt into tenant-specific alerts.
